blurb:
Victor's foster dad leaves the TV on for him when he goes out. That detail tells you basically everything you need to know about how this Bulldog mix has settled into his foster home, and how quickly he tends to make people want to take care of him. The volunteers at Mostly Mutts call him a super sweet boy. His whole body wags when it's his turn for attention. He sat perfectly calm through his bath, just soaking up the one-on-one time.

He's five years old, about 44 pounds, went through the Prison Pups training program, and has a genuinely affectionate, playful personality. He can get a little mouthy when he gets excited, which is worth knowing going in, but it's coming from enthusiasm, not aggression. He's a dog who just really, really wants to be part of whatever is happening.

Victor does best as an only dog and would be better matched with teenagers or adults. He's got some strength to him, so younger kids walking him on leash isn't a great setup. He's also working through some leg challenges right now, and his foster is helping him rest and heal, so check his full profile on the Mostly Mutts website for the current medical details before you reach out.

Submit an adoption inquiry at mostlymutts.org and ask about Victor to get started.

scoring_notes:
• The TV-left-on detail is an instant emotional hook — it signals deep foster attachment and gives readers a vivid, human picture of who Victor is
• Active medical situation with leg challenges adds a layer of complexity that both increases urgency and requires careful reader messaging to avoid dampening interest
• Prison Pups graduate and foster-settled, but only-dog requirement plus ongoing health needs narrow the eligible adopter pool, extending his likely wait and warranting feature placement

blurb:
Eleven years old and still has a spring in his step. Meeko is a 33-pound Jack Russell/Greyhound mix who came through animal control and has been soaking up attention from foster volunteers ever since. He is, by every account, a genuinely delightful little guy.

He'll climb right into your lap if you give him the chance. He makes grateful sighing sounds during baths. He's spunky and playful and vocal enough that condo living probably isn't the right fit, because when Meeko wants your attention, he's going to let you know. That's not a flaw. That's personality. If you want a quiet, undemanding dog who blends into the furniture, Meeko is not your guy. If you want a dog who is actively, enthusiastically happy to be alive and near you, he might be exactly right.

He does best as an only dog and would do well with teenagers or adults. He's shown some prey drive around small animals, so cats would be a gamble. What he wants is a quieter home where he can be your person's dog, fully and completely.

Reach out to Mostly Mutts through their website to start an inquiry and schedule a meet with Meeko.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• At eleven years old with an animal-control intake background, Meeko carries the highest urgency profile in this batch — senior dogs from AC placements face the longest odds
• The 'grateful sighing sounds during baths' moment is the kind of specific, tender detail that stops readers mid-scroll and drives emotional engagement
• Narrow placement criteria — only dog, no cats, vocal temperament, not condo-friendly — means he needs the newsletter spotlight more than most to find his right match

blurb:
Nine years old, 64 pounds, and apparently has not gotten the memo that senior dogs are supposed to slow down. Bolton is a Hound/Boxer mix who came into Mostly Mutts underweight and rough around the edges, but you'd never know it now. He completed the Prison Pups immersive training program, landed himself a foster home, and his foster family describes him as a sweet guy who lights up every room he walks into.

He's got this move where he runs straight at another dog, then takes off in the opposite direction hoping they'll chase him. Tag. He invented it. When he's not doing that, he's got his nose to the ground working out exactly what happened in your backyard over the last 48 hours. And when the sniffing and the running are done, he is genuinely happy to just sit next to you and do nothing. That balance is hard to find.

Bolton does great with dogs who like to play and is good with kids around 8 to 12 years old. No cats, and toddlers would be better off with a smaller dog since Bolton could accidentally bump them over just by being excited. He's a big, goofy, loving guy who had a hard start and deserves a soft landing.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Submit an adoption inquiry through their website and ask about Bolton to get the process started.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Came in underweight and rough, completed a Prison Pups program, and emerged as a joyful senior — a redemption arc readers will champion
• The self-invented tag game and backyard sniffing detail give him instant personality that makes him memorable and shareable
• Senior dog at nine years old who arrived in poor condition signals a meaningful shelter stay; age alone makes him a statistically harder placement and raises urgency

blurb:
Pumps is the shyest one of her litter, and her foster is upfront about it. She hangs back. She watches. She takes longer than her siblings to decide she trusts you. If you're looking for a kitten who runs up to greet strangers, she's probably not it — at least not on day one.

But she's also two and a half months old and about two pounds of pure curiosity. She wants to know what's going on. She loves chasing toys, climbing everything, finding the best lookout spots, and roughhousing with her siblings until everyone's exhausted. The shyness is real, and so is everything underneath it.

She's litter trained and has been living in the Kitty Room at the shelter, so you can go meet her in person. She gets along great with the other cats she's been raised with and held her own just fine around a foster-home ferret. She'd do best with older kids who move calmly and adults who are okay letting her set the pace. The payoff for patience is a playful, curious little sidekick who picked you on her own terms.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Stop by the shelter or visit their website to connect.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• The 'shyest of the litter' angle creates a quiet underdog narrative that resonates with readers who appreciate patience-rewarded bonds
• Her in-shelter placement in the Kitty Room enables easy walk-in meetups, lowering the barrier to adoption and boosting newsletter conversion potential
• Still very young with no strong signals of extended wait; urgency is moderate and largely dependent on her shyness making her harder to place than siblings

blurb:
Part of a shoe-themed litter at Mostly Mutts, Loafer is a two-and-a-half-month-old tuxedo kitten who came in weighing about two pounds and has been getting bigger by the week. He's been with a foster family since birth, and by all accounts he and his siblings have turned into a great group of kittens.

He's a little shy when you first meet him. He'll hang back and watch from a safe spot while he figures you out. But here's the thing — he's also incredibly curious and doesn't actually want to miss anything. Give him a little time and let him come to you, and you'll get the real Loafer: playful, adventurous, into climbing anything he can reach, and absolutely obsessed with chasing toys and wrestling with his kitten buddies. His foster mom says he goes until everyone's worn out.

He's litter trained and gets along great with his siblings. He's also proven he can coexist peacefully with a ferret, which honestly earns some bonus points. He'd probably love having another young cat around to keep up with. Older kids who know how to handle a small kitten would be a good fit. Dogs are unknown.

Reach out to Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw to set up a meet.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• High adoptability ceiling — young, playful, litter-trained kitten with a charming shy-then-wild personality arc that appeals broadly
• The ferret coexistence detail is a memorable, lighthearted hook that stands out in a crowded kitten field
• Very young and recently arrived, suggesting low urgency; limited wait time reduces newsletter priority relative to longer-stay candidates

blurb:
Boots has had a year. She lost her home when a family member passed away, got taken in by a good neighbor, found her way to Mostly Mutts, and then — surprise — turned out to be pregnant. She raised four kittens in foster care, watched them find homes one by one, and now it's finally her turn. She's three years old, about six pounds, and a tuxedo cat with a very clear sense of who she is.

She's not a lap cat who's going to glue herself to you. She likes doing her own thing, and when she's ready for attention, she'll come find you. Pets, treats, maybe a lap for a little while — on her schedule. Her foster has figured out her rhythm and says once you learn it, she's great to live with.

The one thing worth knowing: she'll give a little nip if she gets overstimulated during petting. Not aggressive, just her way of saying she's done. Her foster learned to read her signals and now they're both happy. Because of that, she'd do best in a home with adults or older kids who'll respect her limits. Cats-welcome household is a bonus. Dogs are unknown.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. You can find Boots at the shelter or reach out through their website to start the process.

scoring_notes:
• Emotionally rich journey — lost her home, raised four kittens, now waiting alone — gives readers an immediate reason to root for her
• Her independent personality and clear behavioral signals make her a realistic, relatable match for adult cat households
• Strong urgency signal: she's been through an entire pregnancy and fostering cycle, meaning she has waited longer than almost any cat in this batch
